main_text.l: nos Evangelij facti participes,jam dudum Opt.Max. creatorem & Salvatorem suum, nobiscum in libertate gaudioque Spiritus Sancti colere potuissent. Cognoscemus autem facile magnitudinem hujus mali & caecitatis hujus gravitatem, si lucem quae eos circumfulget & pondus circumstantium veri Dei indiciorum aspiciamus.Nam aliqua adhuc in ipsis ad veri Dei cognitionem aptitudine residua, fieri non posse videtur, ut non advertant radios emicantes, ex hac tam rara & varia rerum proprietate, quae creatorem suum unicum sapientissimum & optimum praedicant: plane-que licet quibusdam ex illis evulsus animae foret oculus, quem cernere in arcanis non possent,in quotidiana saltem scelerum manifestorum vindicta contrectarent; & in paterna pro humano genere sollicitudine, qua terrae fontes, femini imbrem, fegeti solem inducit, caecorum more, quem visu non percipiunt, tactu deprehenderent, si sola caecitate laborarent. Iam vero majus malum videtur & atrocius, plane enim aut sensu destituti, omnemque facultatem ad Dei cognitionem paratam, deposuisse; aut quod multo perniciosius, ex natura conceptam ejus notitiam, atque reverentiam, violenter excutere, assumpto Satanae tanæ

page.notes: Printed text ends with the fragment "tanæ" at the foot of the page; the sentence continues on the next page, so no catchword is given. The printed "fuum", "fenfu", "depofuiffe" and "affumpto" are transcribed with plain s, as "suum", "sensu", "deposuisse" and "assumpto". The line-end hyphens in "plane-que" and "reveren-tiam" are kept as printed; "reverentiam" is a line break across these words. The word "Satanae" is printed with a bare final ae; "tanæ" is the printed fragment at the line end. The line "non poffent,in" and the line "pondus" are transcribed as printed. No printing errors were corrected.
